structures.pattern: Topic は + Object が/を + Verb (end)
structures.title: Basic SOV sentence order
structures.explanation: Japanese is Subject-Object-Verb: the topic (は) leads, objects follow, and the verb closes the sentence. Modifiers always come before what they modify, so the meaning builds toward the final verb.
structures.ex2_target: 彼女は毎朝コーヒーを飲みます。

structures.title: Polite present or future tense
structures.explanation: The ます form is the polite non-past, covering both present habits and future plans. Attach ます to the verb stem (食べ→食べます). Context or a time word decides present vs future.
structures.ex1_target: 毎日日本語を勉強します。
structures.ex2_ref: Tomorrow I will go to Kyoto.

structures.title: Polite past tense
structures.explanation: Change ます to ました to make the polite past. It states that an action was completed. The rest of the sentence order is unchanged.
structures.ex2_target: 先週、友達に会いました。
structures.ex2_ref: I met a friend last week.

structures.title: Polite negative (present/future)
structures.explanation: Replace ます with ません for the polite negative — 'do not' or 'will not'. The past negative is ませんでした. Use it to decline or state what you don't do.
structures.ex1_target: 私はお酒を飲みません。
structures.ex2_target: 今日は仕事に行きません。
structures.ex2_ref: I'm not going to work today.

structures.title: Polite 'A is B' nominal sentence
structures.explanation: です links a noun to the topic, meaning 'is/am/are'. Its past is でした, negative is じゃありません. There is no separate verb 'to be' for simple identity — です carries it.

structures.title: Polite request 'please do'
structures.explanation: Take the て form of a verb and add ください to politely ask someone to do something. For a negative request ('please don't'), use 〜ないでください.
structures.ex1_target: ゆっくり話してください。
structures.ex2_target: ここに名前を書いてください。

structures.title: Ongoing action or continuing state
structures.explanation: て + います marks an action in progress ('is ~ing') or, with change-of-state verbs, a resulting condition ('lives', 'is married'). It is the closest thing to the English present continuous.
structures.ex2_target: 姉は東京で働いています。
structures.ex2_ref: My older sister works in Tokyo.

structures.title: Expressing 'I want to do'
structures.explanation: Attach たい to the verb stem to state your own desire to do something. It conjugates like an い-adjective (たくない, たかった). The object may take が or を.
structures.ex1_target: 日本語を勉強したいです。
structures.ex2_ref: I want to go to a hot spring.

structures.pattern: A より B のほうが + adj
structures.title: Comparing two things
structures.explanation: より marks the thing compared against (the 'than' item), and Bのほうが highlights the one that is more. Word order is flexible, but のほうが always attaches to the favored item.
structures.ex1_target: 犬より猫のほうが好きです。
structures.ex1_ref: I like cats more than dogs.
structures.ex2_target: バスより電車のほうが速いです。
structures.ex2_ref: The train is faster than the bus.

structures.pattern: Place に Noun が あります / います
structures.title: Stating existence and location
structures.explanation: あります is used for inanimate things, います for living things. The location takes に, and the thing that exists takes が. It answers 'what/who is there?'.
structures.ex1_target: 机の上に本があります。
structures.ex1_ref: There is a book on the desk.
structures.ex2_ref: There are children in the park.

structures.title: Relative (noun-modifying) clause
structures.explanation: A whole clause in plain form can modify a noun by sitting directly before it — no relative pronoun needed. The modified noun is what the clause describes.
structures.ex1_target: ここに住んでいる人は親切です。
structures.ex1_ref: The person who lives here is kind.
structures.ex2_target: 母が作った料理はおいしいです。
structures.ex2_ref: The food my mother made is delicious.

structures.title: Giving a reason with 'because'
structures.explanation: から follows the reason clause and means 'because/so'. The reason comes first, the consequence second — the reverse of English 'X because Y'. ので is a softer, more formal alternative.
structures.ex1_target: 雨が降っているから、行きません。
structures.ex1_ref: Because it's raining, I won't go.
structures.ex2_target: 時間がないから、急ぎましょう。
structures.ex2_ref: We have no time, so let's hurry.

structures.pattern: Object が Verb-れる/られる (passive)
structures.title: The passive voice
structures.explanation: The passive れる/られる shows the subject is acted upon, often to their inconvenience. The doer, when mentioned, is marked by に. Ichidan verbs take られる, godan verbs take れる.
structures.ex2_target: 先生に褒められました。
structures.ex2_ref: I was praised by the teacher.

structures.title: Superlative 'the most'
structures.explanation: 一番 (ichiban, 'number one') before an adjective makes the superlative — 'the most / the -est'. The category compared is marked with で ('among/in').
structures.ex1_target: 富士山が日本で一番高いです。
structures.ex1_ref: Mt. Fuji is the highest in Japan.
structures.ex2_target: このレストランが町で一番おいしいです。
structures.ex2_ref: This restaurant is the tastiest in town.

structures.title: Expressing obligation 'must'
structures.explanation: Built from the negative conditional 〜なければ plus なりません ('it won't do'), this pattern means 'must / have to'. The casual contraction is 〜なきゃ.
structures.ex1_target: 今行かなければなりません。
structures.ex2_target: 薬を飲まなければなりません。

structures.title: Conditional 'if/when'
structures.explanation: Add たら to the plain past form to make the most versatile conditional, good for 'if' and 'once/when' for future one-time events. The result clause follows.
structures.ex1_target: 時間があったら、行きます。
structures.ex1_ref: If I have time, I'll go.
structures.ex2_target: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
structures.ex2_ref: When you arrive at the station, please call me.
